heading: Rooted in Service, Ready to Lead
text: Dr. Kedner Maxime’s journey is the story of the American Dream built entirely on faith, resilience, and hard work. Arriving in the United States from Haiti in April 1981 as an 18-year-old student, he spoke little English and started with nothing. He washed dishes in local restaurants for $2.50 an hour and mowed grass on hot Florida golf courses for $4.50 an hour, working up to three jobs at a time to provide for his family. He has never forgotten the struggle of living paycheck-to-paycheck, and that is why he is stepping up to fight for you.

heading: Rooted in Service, Ready to Lead
text: For over thirty years, Dr. Maxime has stood in the trenches with Florida’s 20th District. As the founder of Advantage Tax Firm Consulting Services (since 1996), he has sat across kitchen tables from thousands of local taxpayers—helping them navigate tax codes, start businesses, and achieve the dream of U.S. citizenship. As a pastor for 16 years at L’Eglise la Voix du Salut and a trusted WLQY 1320AM radio host for two decades, his leadership has always been driven by a simple, unyielding creed: Service over Politics, Solutions over Promises.

heading: On the Issues
text: Too many District 20 workers are stuck in jobs that don't pay enough to live on. Too many workers who want more can't afford the training to get there. And too many young people watch good jobs go somewhere else because the pipeline between our schools and our employers isn't connected. Economic security isn't a slogan — it's whether you can pay rent, save for retirement, and take a day off when you're sick.

heading: Solutions
text: Dr. Maxime will fight for the jobs, training, and protections District 20 workers deserve:
Invest in workforce training aligned to South Florida's real industries — healthcare, construction, logistics, hospitality, and skilled trades.
Expand apprenticeship pathways so workers can earn while they learn.
Support fair wages that keep pace with the actual cost of living in South Florida.
Defend earned benefits — Social Security, Medicare, and workplace protections — from cuts.
Protect the right to organize and negotiate for fair pay and safe conditions.
District 20 workers deserve dignity, security, and a real shot at a better life — not just a check that never quite covers the bills.

heading: Immigration
text: Dr. Kedner Maxime's balanced plan — secure borders, fair laws, a legal path for those who follow the law, and family reunification.

heading: On the Issues
text: A different kind of voice on immigration

heading: On the Issues
text: For more than 30 years, Dr. Maxime has worked with immigrant families across South Florida — as an accountant, a U.S. citizenship service consultant, and a pastor. He has sat across the table from families navigating a complex system, helped them understand their rights, and helped them become proud American citizens. He knows this issue not from a talking point, but from a lifetime of walking with people through it.

heading: On the Issues
text: The system isn't working for anyone. It isn't working for families waiting years for a decision. It isn't working for communities dealing with the consequences of chaos at the border. And it isn't working for the people who want to do things the right way and can't find one.

heading: Solutions
text: Dr. Maxime believes we can have both security and compassion — and that we should stop pretending we have to choose:
Secure borders that protect our communities.
A pathway to citizenship for those who contribute to our society.
Family-reunification policies that keep families together.
A clear, fair pathway to legal permanent residency for those who follow the law.
Fair, faster processing so people who follow the rules aren't punished for doing so.
"We are a nation of laws and a nation of compassion."

heading: Healthcare
text: Dr. Kedner Maxime's plan to lower prescription drug costs, protect pre-existing conditions, expand access, and strengthen community health centers.

heading: On the Issues
text: As a pastor for 16 years, Dr. Maxime has stood with families in their greatest joys and their deepest struggles. He has met seniors rationing insulin because they can't afford a full dose. He has met working parents who skip their own doctor visits so their children can be seen. He has met families driven into bankruptcy by a single medical emergency. In the richest nation on earth, that is not acceptable.

heading: Solutions
text: Dr. Maxime will bring that ground-level view to Washington and fight for a healthcare system that actually serves the people paying for it:
Lower prescription drug costs so no senior has to choose between insulin and groceries.
Protect coverage for people with pre-existing conditions — no one should lose care because of a diagnosis outside their control.
Expand access to affordable care for working families, the self-employed, and small-business owners.
Strengthen the community health centers that serve our most vulnerable neighbors — the safety net working families rely on.
Bring transparency to hospital and insurance billing so families aren't blindsided by charges they never agreed to.
Healthcare is not a luxury. It's a right. And in Congress, Dr. Maxime will fight for that right — for every family in District 20.

heading: Education
text: Dr. Maxime plans to work to raise school funding and teacher pay, expand vocational training, and build real career pathways for District 20's young people.

heading: On the Issues
text: Dr. Maxime spent 25 years teaching Sunday school in Broward County churches. He knows the difference a great teacher makes in a child's life — and he knows what it costs a community when our schools are underfunded and our teachers underpaid. In District 20, too many young people, especially in underserved communities, aren't getting the education and training they need to build the future they deserve.

heading: Solutions
text: Every child deserves a real shot — not one that depends on their zip code. Dr. Maxime will fight to:
Raise public-school funding so classrooms have the resources, materials, and support they need.
Expand vocational and technical training so students who don't take a four-year path still have a real path.
Raise teacher salaries so we can recruit and keep the great educators our children deserve.
Build real pathways — apprenticeships, dual enrollment, industry partnerships — so a diploma opens doors, not just closes a chapter.
Empower both our young men and young women with the skills, mentorship, and opportunities to succeed.
Our young people are our future. They deserve an investment in that future — regardless of zip code.

heading: Lower Costs
text: Dr. Kedner Maxime's plan to lower everyday costs for District 20 families — housing, groceries, healthcare — and open real pathways to ownership.

heading: On the Issues
text: Working families across South Florida are getting squeezed from every direction. Rent and mortgages keep climbing. Groceries cost more every trip. Insurance premiums keep going up. And a single medical bill can wipe out a year of savings. Too many families are working harder than ever and still falling behind.

heading: Solutions
text: Dr. Maxime will fight for policies that lower the everyday costs squeezing District 20 households — and open real pathways so working families can move from paycheck to equity:
Support responsible federal spending and fair competition that brings inflation down and stops price gouging.
Expand affordable housing so working families, seniors, and young people can find a home they can actually afford.
Open pathways to ownership, equity, and generational wealth — because the goal isn't just surviving the paycheck, it's building something that lasts.
Protect Social Security, Medicare, and the earned benefits working people paid into their whole lives.
Back responsible first-time-homebuyer assistance so more District 20 families move from renting to owning.
Service over politics. Solutions over promises.

heading: On the Issues
text: Why small business is District 20's backbone

heading: On the Issues
text: The corner store. The family restaurant. The two-truck landscaping outfit. The immigrant-owned bakery that anchors the neighborhood. Small businesses are how District 20 builds — how families move from working for someone else to owning their own future. But too many entrepreneurs are drowning in paperwork, shut out of capital, and losing ground to national chains that get every break in the book.

heading: Solutions
text: Dr. Maxime spent 30 years as an accountant sitting across the table from small-business owners — helping them make sense of taxes, permits, payroll, and cash flow. He knows exactly what breaks a small business and what saves one. In Congress, he'll fight to:
Cut federal red tape and simplify small-business tax filing so owners can spend time serving customers, not fighting paperwork.
Expand SBA lending and micro-lending so capital reaches the entrepreneurs who need it most.
Support minority- and immigrant-owned businesses that anchor District 20 neighborhoods.
Protect small businesses from predatory fees, hidden bank charges, and payment-processor gouging.
Level the playing field so small businesses aren't crushed by unfair competition from national players.
If you're building a business in District 20, Dr. Maxime is fighting to make sure Washington helps you — not blocks you.

heading: On the Issues
text: Dr. Maxime taught Sunday school in Broward County churches for 25 years. He knows District 20's young people — their talent, their dreams, and the walls too many of them run into. Right now, too many students are graduating with debt that dictates the rest of their lives. Too many young workers are locked out of trades they'd thrive in. And too many families are watching their kids leave South Florida because opportunity keeps moving somewhere else.

heading: Solutions
text: Every young person in District 20 deserves a real path forward — whether that path runs through a university, a trade, or an apprenticeship. Dr. Maxime will fight to:
Expand Pell grants and make community college genuinely affordable.
Grow apprenticeship and vocational pathways so a trade is a real career, not a fallback.
Protect and strengthen trade schools and technical training programs.
Invest in mentorship, internships, and workforce partnerships that keep District 20 talent in District 20.
Provide targeted student-debt relief for teachers, nurses, and public-service workers District 20 needs.
Our young people are our future. They deserve investment in that future — with a real path, real support, and a real chance to build a life right here at home.

heading: On the Issues
text: Working District 20 families are earning paychecks — and too few are ever building anything with them. Rent goes to someone else's asset. Retirement savings feel out of reach. And the wealth that gets passed from one generation to the next never quite gets started. That gap between working hard and getting ahead is why so many families feel stuck no matter how many hours they put in.

heading: Solutions
text: For more than 30 years, Dr. Maxime has worked as an accountant — sitting across the table from families trying to make the numbers work. He knows the difference between earning and owning, and he'll fight for policies that help working families cross that line:
Expand responsible first-time-homebuyer assistance so renting doesn't have to be forever.
Protect and grow retirement savings vehicles that working people can actually use.
Defend Social Security and Medicare — the earned benefits working people paid into.
Back tax policies that reward saving and ownership for working households, not just top earners.
Support small-dollar investing and financial education so families build wealth on their own terms.
The goal isn't just to survive the paycheck. The goal is to build something that lasts — for your family and for the next generation.

heading: Meet Dr. Maxime
text: Pastor. Immigrant. Father. Public servant. Dr. Kedner Maxime has spent three decades in the trenches with District 20 families, and he's ready to fight for them in Washington.

heading: MEET DR. MAXIME
text: A Servant Leader, Not a Career Politician

heading: MEET DR. MAXIME
text: For over thirty years, Dr. Kedner Maxime has not been sitting in backrooms making political deals. He has been sitting across kitchen tables from families like yours in Florida’s 20th Congressional District—listening to their struggles, helping them navigate complex systems, and standing with them in their greatest trials.

heading: MEET DR. MAXIME
text: As a pastor, a local businessman, a father, and a community caretaker, Dr. Maxime’s run for Congress is not driven by political ambition. It is a direct continuation of his thirty-year ministry of service.

heading: MEET DR. MAXIME
text: "I’m not running because I’m a politician. All my life I’ve been a servant leader—and I believe you deserve a representative who actually shows up, listens, and fights for practical results."

He knew what it felt like to go home exhausted and sweat-drenched, working up to three jobs at a time to provide a better life for his loved ones and fund his children’s futures.

heading: Why leave the comfort of the pulpit to step into the dirty world of politics?
text: This is a question I get asked a lot. My answer is simple: I am not leaving service behind; I am expanding where I serve. My run for Congress is a direct extension of my ministry. How can I stand behind the four walls of a church and preach about love and justice while watching our neighbors squeeze to buy groceries, seniors ration insulin they can't afford, and working families live in fear of eviction or deportation? When you see injustice and chaos in your community, you don't stay silent. You step up to fill the gap.
